chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who consumes usury (riba), while he believes it is prohibited for him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not harm him until he consumes it deliberately. So when he consumes it deliberately, he is in the status which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has spoken of.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who eats usury while believing it is haram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that consuming riba while believing it is forbidden constitutes a sin of omission rather than disbelief, sparing the individual from the severe Quranic penalty until they consume it deliberately with conviction. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the interplay between belief (yaqin) and action (fi'l), where deliberate consumption despite prior knowledge triggers the specific divine warning. The ruling underscores that the severity of the sin escalates from mere transgression to a state akin to those who 'declare war against Allah' when the act becomes intentional and conscious.
